title: Spin mixing induced dynamics of spinor solitons in $F=1$ Bose Einstein condensates
authors: T. Panagos, A. Romero-Ros, G. C. Katsimiga, P. Schmelcher, P. G. Kevrekidis
abstract: We explore soliton interactions in a homogeneous spinor $F=1$ Bose Einstein Condensate (BEC) in the presence of a magnetic field, focusing on dark bright dark and bright dark bright configurations. We investigate how these interactions depend on the phase differences among bright solitons and their influence during the dynamics. Our findings align with prior non spinor results, i.e., repulsion among in phase bright solitons and attraction among out of phase pairs in self repulsive atomic BECs. The potential bright soliton attraction, added to the short range repulsion of dark dark soliton interactions, can lead to bound states. However, we find that these bound states break in the presence of spinor interactions due to the particle exchange dynamics between the hyperfine states of the components. Additonally, we develop an effective classical model to describe the soliton dynamics, using a Lagrangian approach. The accuracy of the model is tested by comparing it against numerical simulations. Our results suggest that the proposed model captures the essential features of soliton behavior in the presence of spin interactions, and provides congruent soliton trajectories and interspecies particle exchange dynamics in most of the cases.
summary: This paper analyzes the interaction dynamics of spinor solitons in $F=1$ BECs, examining configurations like dark-bright-dark. The research develops an effective Lagrangian model whose predictions are tested against numerical simulations. It reveals that while attraction can form bound states, spin interactions cause these to break via particle exchange, highlighting the complexity beyond simple non-spinor models.
main_problem: The study investigates the spin-mixing-induced dynamics of spinor solitons within $F=1$ Bose Einstein Condensates (BECs), focusing on interactions between dark and bright soliton configurations.
main_result: While initial attraction can lead to bound states, these states break down due to particle exchange dynamics induced by spin interactions. An effective classical model successfully captures the essential features of soliton behavior in most cases.
method: The authors employ numerical simulations using Runge-Kutta integrators and develop an effective classical model based on a Lagrangian approach to describe the time evolution of variational parameters.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a 1D spinor $F=1$ BEC governed by dimensionless spinor Gross-Pitaevskii equations (SGPEs) for three hyperfine states. The dynamics are analyzed in terms of dark and bright solitons interacting via spin-mixing terms.
key_observables: Soliton densities ($|\Psi_m|^2$), interspecies particle exchange, effective interaction strength (repulsive/attractive), and variational parameters ($\xi(t)$, $\varphi(t)$).
important_parameters: Spin-dependent coefficient $g_s$ (determining F or AF interactions), initial phase difference ($\Delta\phi$), and the quadratic Zeeman term ($q$).
main_assumptions: The effective model relies on the adiabatic approximation, which breaks down when large soliton overlaps occur, particularly in out-of-phase (OP) configurations.
figures_summary: Figures compare the predictions of the effective classical model against numerical simulations for both In-Phase (IP) and Out-of-Phase (OP) interactions, showing fidelity metrics and particle number evolution.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the governing SGPEs and analyzes basic soliton interactions. It then develops an effective Lagrangian model to describe two-soliton dynamics, comparing its predictions against detailed numerical simulations for various phase configurations.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles complex non-linear dynamics in ultracold atomic systems, specifically addressing how internal spin degrees of freedom modify classical soliton interactions and lead to particle redistribution.
